narrative: Material PL2__M31E3DB3 shows smooth, normally distributed daily demand averaging 19,648 units with a CV of 0.24 and no statistically significant trend over the observation period. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.50), driven primarily by transport variability across three clusters, warranting a robust safety buffer. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-based order quantity of 293,053 units and a 43,106-unit safety stock achieves the 95% service level at minimal holding cost, while the current SAP zero-safety-stock setting is structurally insufficient.
warnings: 15 demand observations flagged as outliers (winsorised at IQR bounds); likely reflect partial-day or batch-entry records.
Lead time CV of 0.5013 exceeds unstable threshold; dominant driver is transport variance at 70%.
SAP safety stock is currently 0, providing no protection against demand or lead time variability.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and near-normally distributed with continuous non-zero flow, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. The EOQ balances ordering and holding costs, the reorder point embeds lead-time uncertainty, and the policy maps directly to SAP MRP reorder-point materials.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity constraint binds: SS (43,106) + Q (293,053) = 336,159 units, which is 71.4% of the 470,820-unit storage limit. Ample headroom exists.
